why_it_matters: Hard cap preserves a small reusable art vocabulary.
Every building should be skinnable without altering footprint/collision.
Enough recurring families to create district identity without asset sprawl.
Vertical road infrastructure should be visible but not clutter every road.
GWB and waterfront landmarks should not fall back to generic road/building art.
Suspension-cable visuals are independent cosmetic geometry over the semantic bridge deck.
Night mood should come from local light pools, not a single dark filter.
Large semantic footprints should break into richer visual masses without changing collision.
Alleys/lightwells/cut-through cues provide memorable top-down layout structure without copying another map.
Dense reusable dressing improves urban richness without increasing the 100-object archetype budget.
Every non-motorway road should provide a pedestrian edge so road-walking is rarely necessary.
Most ordinary streets should retain a strong bright sidewalk/curb band; narrow trunk sidewalks may be intentionally slimmer.
Road hierarchy is reviewed structurally, never by pixel registration.
Dense recurring props support the gritty callback atmosphere.
